title: Babies are born with fontanelles, the soft spots between skull bones
summary: Babies are born with fontanelles, open spaces between skull bones that MedlinePlus also calls soft spots.
body: MedlinePlus says an infant skull's bones are held by strong fibrous sutures, and the spaces that remain open are fontanelles, sometimes called soft spots. Two are usual: one on the top of the middle of the head, just forward of center, and one at the back of the middle of the head. The page says the posterior space usually closes by age 1 to 2 months and may already be closed at birth, while the anterior space usually closes sometime within 7 to 19 months. The gaps let the brain grow and let the bones overlap during birth. Usually is the page's word. These times are not a deadline for one baby.

sources.title: Cranial sutures
sources.author: MedlinePlus
sources.note: Supports fontanelles as open spaces also called soft spots, the two usual sites, the usual closing ages, and the role in brain growth and birth.
